{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (HDI / Company Internet Site Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — findings, redlines and walk-away exposure

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The commercial architecture is a revenue-share hosting and site-development arrangement, and several of its terms are favourable to us: there is no MFN obligation, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment (fees accrue only on Net Sales above the $11,000 monthly floor), no non-solicitation covenant binding us, New York law governs (§ 10.5), and HDI carries a heavier two-year post-term restriction under § 6.3.

The problem is what the Agreement omits. There is **no indemnification of any kind**, **no intellectual property ownership provision**, **no limitation of liability or cap**, **no performance warranty**, **no transition-assistance or data-return obligation**, and **no insurance covenant** — this in an arrangement where HDI builds and hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and customer data. Three of those gaps (vendor IP indemnity, insurance for a vendor processing Customer Data, and the effective exclusion of our affiliates and contractors from the § 1.4 grant via § 10.3) sit in walk-away territory under the playbook.

Separately, the exit economics are materially off-market for us. Our convenience right in § 4.1 is real on its face but is priced by the § 4.2 Termination Payment — 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales over $800,000, uncapped, payable by the Company alone and triggered by essentially any Company termination. Combined with the indefinite § 6.1 exclusivity (auto-renewing term, no performance-based release), our ability to leave a failing engagement is illusory. These are our principal negotiation asks alongside the missing risk-allocation provisions.

One finding (non-solicitation) did not clear verification and is carried as **needs review** rather than as a conclusion; one finding (licence scope) was repaired on verification.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | New § 9(c) proposed (Warranties) | No indemnity, hold-harmless or defence language anywhere; § 9 is corporate reps plus the Globix carve-out only. Walk-away territory given HDI supplies software, technology and hosting. Preferred HDI indemnity inserted (third-party IP, breach of law, HDI-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation mechanics, sited in § 9 so it survives under § 10.7. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | New § 5.5 proposed | No ownership or assignment clause; nothing states who owns the Site, the deliverables we fund, our Content or customer data, and there is no licence back of HDI platform IP. Mitigant: no assignment of Company IP or data to HDI and § 10.2 disclaims co-ownership. Proposed § 5.5 gives Company ownership plus HDI assignment, HDI retains background IP, perpetual royalty-free licence back. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | New § 10.9 proposed | No cap, no exclusion of consequential damages; the only "liability" references are in the no-joint-venture clause (§ 10.2). Both parties, including us, face unlimited exposure. Inserted mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees / USD 1,000,000, mutual indirect-damages exclusion, uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirmation that our § 3 / § 4.2 payment obligations are not capped damages. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 6.1 (with § 4.1, § 4.2, § 1.6) | Category is defined, but the restriction runs for the whole term and § 4.1 auto-renews annually, so it is potentially indefinite; the only exit is terminating the Agreement, which can trigger the § 4.2 Termination Payment. No performance-based release. Fails the fallback and approaches walk-away. Given HDI's reciprocal § 6.3 restriction benefits us, we propose the fallback: cap our restriction at 12 months from the Effective Date with automatic release on HDI's failure to hit the operational date or any service level, delivery date or performance obligation. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 4.2 | Stipulated sum payable by us on any Company termination: (trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2, in eight quarterly instalments. Measured against gross Net Sales rather than fees and uncapped — far beyond three months' fees (illustratively ~$600,000 vs ~$140,000 at $2M annual Net Sales) — and triggered even by ordinary § 4.1 non-renewal or termination for HDI's default (only the narrow § 1.6 launch carve-out applies). Proposed deletion; three-month fee cap available as fallback. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 4.1 / § 4.2(a) | Notice mechanics (90 days against a one-year auto-renewing term) sit at the fallback and are not flagged. The material failure is the price of our exit under § 4.2(a), which is uncapped and bites on any Company termination other than § 1.6 launch failure, rendering the convenience right illusory. Proportionate edit: cap the Termination Payment at three months' fees and confirm it is not payable where we terminate for HDI's failure to launch or breach; § 4.2(c) instalment schedule unaffected. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant (at fallback) | § 6.1 (with § 6.2, § 4.1, § 8(b)) | Sits at the fallback and is not redlined: scope limited to defined Deerskin Products plus named competitors; term-only with no post-term tail on us; effectively capped within 12 months via the § 4.1 one-year term and 90-day exit; carve-outs for our closeout website, Joan Cook Catalog products and the grandfathered Globix Agreement. Field of use covers only similar Internet projects, leaving catalog, retail and sourcing unrestricted. Noted, not flagged: "companies similar to" is elastic and there is no acquisitions/internal-development carve-out — to be tightened only if the Agreement is reopened. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation *(verification: repaired)* | § 1.4 with § 10.3 | The § 1.4 access/use grant runs to "the Company" alone — no affiliates, no contractors, no notice mechanic — and § 10.3 affirmatively provides that "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement," which excludes them with no path to add them (the rule's walk-away trigger). § 10.3 is otherwise a standard binding-effect clause and does not itself grant an affirmative M&A transfer right. Redline extends § 1.4 to affiliates, contractors acting on our behalf and a successor by merger/acquisition/asset sale, and carves them out of § 10.3; affiliates-on-written-notice offered as fallback. Grant is not stated to be revocable, so no revocability edit needed. |
| Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 10.3 | Bare successors-and-assigns clause. Positives: no prohibition on Company assignment and no change-of-control trigger anywhere, so HDI cannot exit or re-price on our change of control. But the clause is silent on consent both ways, leaving HDI free to assign this hosting engagement — and our data obligations — to anyone, including a competitor. Redline adds our affiliate/successor carve-out plus a reasonable-consent gate and no-competitor limit on HDI, leaving the binding language intact. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 | Notice (30 days), business-hours conduct, cost allocation and the narrow scope (payment-calculation records held by our General Manager, no system access) meet or exceed the preferred position. The single failure is the absence of any frequency limit — unlimited inspections fall below the fallback and into walk-away territory. Minimal edit: cap at once per twelve months. That the inspector is HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor is noted only, as HDI is bound by § 8.2 confidentiality. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 9 (new § 9(c) proposed) | § 9 contains only mutual corporate reps (p0056–p0057) and the Globix acknowledgement (p0058). Nothing in §§ 1.1–1.8 or § 5 warrants professional and workmanlike performance, conformance to approved specifications, compliance with laws or absence of malicious code, and there is no repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy — below the fallback. Mitigant: no "AS IS" disclaimer, and § 1.6 gives a launch-failure termination right, so not walk-away. Redline inserts preferred § 9(c); shorter conformance period available as fallback. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 4 (new § 4.3 proposed) | § 4 covers only notice, Termination Date and the Termination Payment; no exit, migration, data return/export or deletion obligation anywhere, and § 8 has no return-or-destroy obligation. In a hosting arrangement where HDI holds our Content, user information and customer data, we would have no right to our data or migration help on exit — below the fallback. Proposed § 4.3: six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, 30-day return in machine-readable format, deletion with written certification. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 4.1 | Successive one-year auto-renewals are acceptable, but the 90-day non-renewal window exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling (just short of walk-away). Shorten to 30 days, with 60 days as fallback. No renewal reminder and no uplift cap are needed here: fees are a share of Net Sales and there is no uplift mechanic. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 10.5 | New York law (our preferred choice), with conflict-of-laws principles disapplied. No foreign venue and no mandatory arbitration anywhere in the document. Only shortfall is the absence of an express exclusive-venue provision naming the New York County courts — a missing sub-element of the preferred wording, noted rather than redlined. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 3 (Fees; Payment) | No MFN, "no less favourable", best-terms or matching language. The only economics are the fixed revenue share in § 3. The § 6.1 exclusivity is an exclusivity term, not MFN pricing, and is handled above. Preferred position; no redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 3.1 (with § 4.1) | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall payment or volume cap. Fees are a pure 30% revenue share above an $11,000 monthly floor, so we pay only on actual sales and owe nothing if the Site earns nothing; the floor benefits us. § 4.1 gives a standing 90-day exit. Noted, not double-flagged: § 4.2 scales with actual sales rather than any shortfall (addressed under LD/T4C), and § 6.1 is a channel restriction (addressed under EXCLUSIVITY). |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Needs review** *(verification: fail)* | § 5.4 / §§ 6, 8, 9, 10 | The review recorded no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binding the Company, based on full reads of §§ 1.4, 5.4, 6, 8, 9 and 10 and targeted searches ("solicit", "hire", "employ", "induce", "personnel", "directly or indirectly"), with only incidental hits in the § 8 confidentiality carve-out (p0051) and the No Joint Venture clause (p0061). The preferred position is no non-solicit on the Customer, so absence would satisfy the rule outright and no redline was made. **Verification did not pass, so we are not treating this as settled** — see Next steps. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 10 (new § 10.9 proposed) | No insurance obligation anywhere; § 10 runs from Notices to Headings/Counterparts without one. HDI develops and hosts the Site and, per § 8.1, accesses our Content, user information and data — a vendor processing Customer Data with no coverage requirement, which is walk-away territory. Inserted preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback flagged for discussion. |

## Walk-away items

These are the points the playbook treats as walk-away territory. We should not sign without movement on them.

1. **No vendor IP indemnity (INDEMN, § 9).** HDI builds and hosts the Site and supplies software and technology; the total absence of an IP-infringement indemnity fails even the fallback.
2. **No insurance for a vendor processing Customer Data (INSURANCE, § 10).** HDI holds our Content, user information and data under § 8.1 with no coverage obligation at all.
3. **Affiliates and contractors affirmatively excluded from the licence (LICENSE, §§ 1.4 and 10.3).** The "no other person shall acquire or have any rights" language in § 10.3 blocks affiliate and contractor use with no mechanism to add them.
4. **Unlimited inspection frequency (AUDIT, § 3.4).** Otherwise a well-drafted clause; the missing frequency cap alone puts it below the fallback and into walk-away territory. This should be a straightforward fix.
5. **Near-walk-away, treat as must-fix in the same breath:** the indefinite § 6.1 exclusivity with no performance-based release (EXCLUSIVITY), and the uncapped Company-only § 4.2 Termination Payment (LD / T4C), which together make exit from a failing engagement impracticable. Also note the complete absence of a liability cap (LOL-CAP), which leaves us, as well as HDI, unlimited.

## Next steps

1. **Re-verify the non-solicitation finding.** The NOSOLICIT check failed verification. Before we rely on the conclusion that no non-solicit binds us, re-run the search across the full document and confirm no restriction sits outside the sections already read. No redline pending that confirmation.
2. **Circulate the redline to HDI** with the four walk-away items and the § 4.2 / § 6.1 exit package presented as our opening position: new §§ 9(c) (indemnity and warranty), 5.5 (IP ownership), 10.9 (liability cap and insurance), 4.3 (transition and data return), the § 3.4 frequency cap, the §§ 1.4 / 10.3 licence extension, the § 10.3 assignment consent gate, and the § 4.1 notice window.
3. **Sequence the commercial asks.** Deletion of § 4.2 is our preferred position; if HDI will not accept deletion, fall back to a three-month fee cap plus confirmation that nothing is payable where we terminate for HDI's failure to launch or breach. On § 6.1, offer the 12-month cap with automatic performance-failure release, leaving HDI's exclusive brand right and § 6.3 intact.
4. **Identify pre-agreed fallbacks for the risk-allocation clauses:** plain 12 months' fees on the liability cap if HDI resists the USD 1,000,000 floor; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M on insurance; a shorter conformance period on the warranty; affiliates-on-written-notice on the licence; 60 days on the renewal window; and a narrow Company indemnity limited to Company-supplied Content if HDI asks for reciprocity.
5. **Confirm operational assumptions with the business** — expected Net Sales trajectory (to size the § 4.2 exposure and the twelve-months'-fees cap), which affiliates and contractors need Site access, and the data we would need returned on exit.
6. **Housekeeping if the Agreement is reopened:** add an exclusive-venue provision naming the New York County courts (§ 10.5), and tighten "companies similar to" plus add an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out in § 6.1. Neither is worth opening on its own."}
